The mole was scared of Lila. He did not want to play with her. He wanted to hide in his hole. He said, "No, no, no! Go away, girl! You are big and loud and scary. You will hurt me and my home. Leave me alone!"

But Lila did not listen to the mole. She thought he was shy and cute. She tried to pick him up and hug him. She said, "Don't be afraid, mole. I will not hurt you. I will be nice to you. You are so soft and warm. You can be my pet."

The mole did not like to be picked up and hugged. He felt trapped and angry. He bit Lila's finger with his sharp teeth. He said, "Let me go, let me go, let me go! You are mean and rude and silly. You do not know how to treat me. I am not your pet. I am a wild animal."

Lila screamed and dropped the mole. She ran to her mom and showed her the bite. She said, "Mom, mom, mom! The mole bit me! It hurt so much. Why did he do that? I just wanted to be his friend."

Her mom looked at the bite and said, "Oh, Lila. You are not lucky. You are foolish. You should not bother the mole. He does not want to be your friend. He wants to be left alone. You should respect his space and his nature. Now we have to go to the doctor and get a shot. Maybe you will learn your lesson."

Lila cried and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, mole. I did not mean to make you mad. I just wondered what you were like. I will not bother you again."

The mole watched Lila and her mom leave. He was glad they were gone. He went back to his hole and said, "Good riddance, girl. You are not welcome in my garden. I am lucky to be a mole. I do not need friends like you."

One day, a fat cat saw a bird on a bush. The cat wanted to catch the bird and eat it. He crept closer and closer to the bush, but the bird saw him and flew away.

"Meow!" the cat cried. He was angry and hungry. He looked around and saw a toy bird on a window sill. The toy bird was red and shiny and made a chirping sound. The cat thought it was a real bird. He jumped on the window sill and grabbed the toy bird with his teeth.

"Hey, that's my toy bird!" a little girl shouted. She ran to the window and saw the cat. She opened the window and tried to take the toy bird back. But the cat was strong and held on to the toy bird. He hissed and scratched the little girl.

"Ow, ow, ow!" the little girl cried. She was hurt and sad. She ran to her mom and told her what happened. Her mom hugged her and gave her a band-aid.

"Mom, the cat took my toy bird. He was mean and bad. I want my toy bird back," the little girl said.

"I'm sorry, honey. That cat was very rude and greedy. He should not have taken your toy bird. Maybe he was lonely and wanted a friend. But he did not know how to ask nicely. He should learn to share and be kind," her mom said.

"Mom, can we replace my toy bird? Can we get a new one?" the little girl asked.

"Of course, honey. We can go to the store and get a new toy bird. But first, let's see if we can find the cat and give him a chance to say sorry. Maybe he will realize his mistake and return your toy bird. Maybe he will want to be your friend. What do you think?" her mom asked.

The little girl thought for a moment. She was still angry and hurt, but she also felt sorry for the cat. Maybe he was not so bad after all. Maybe he just needed some love and care.

"Okay, mom. Let's try to find the cat and talk to him. Maybe we can replace his anger with kindness," the little girl said.

The mom smiled and hugged the little girl. She was proud of her for being brave and forgiving. They went to look for the cat and hoped to make peace with him.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of sharing, kindness, forgiveness, and empathy. It shows that taking something that does not belong to you is wrong and hurts others. It also shows that everyone makes mistakes and deserves a chance to apologize and make amends. It also shows that sometimes the best way to replace something that is lost or broken is to replace it with something that is better or more meaningful, such as a friendship.

"Let's make olive soup!" Tom says. He puts a pot on the stove. He turns on the fire.

"OK!" Mia says. She opens the jar. She pours the olives into the pot. She adds some water and salt.

They stir the soup with a spoon. They smell the soup. It smells good.

"Can we taste it?" Mia asks.

"Sure!" Tom says. He takes a ladle. He fills a bowl with soup. He gives it to Mia.

Mia takes a sip. She makes a face. She spits out the soup. "Yuck! This is bad!" she says.

Tom laughs. He takes the bowl from Mia. He sips the soup. He likes it. He says, "No, this is good! You are silly!"

He drinks more soup. He eats more olives. He does not share with Mia. He eats and eats until the pot is empty.

Mia is angry. She says, "You are greedy! You are mean! You are not my friend!"

Tom does not care. He is full. He is happy. He says, "I don't care! I like olive soup! You are picky! You are not my friend!"

Mia cries. She runs away. She does not want to play with Tom anymore.

Tom feels sick. He ate too much. His tummy hurts. He is chubby. He is alone. He does not have a friend. He is sad. He wishes he shared the soup with Mia. He says, "I am sorry, Mia. Please come back. Please be my friend." But Mia does not hear him. She is gone. The end.

Ben and Mia nod. They do what they want with their fish. Then they hug Dad and say, "Thank you, Dad, for taking us fishing. We had fun." Dad hugs them back and says, "You're welcome, Ben and Mia. I love you." They pack up their poles and go home.

Tom was shocked. He had broken the sword. He felt very sorry. He said, "Oh no, Sam, I was wrong. I was greedy and mean. I should have listened to you. You are wise. You know how to be a good friend. Can you forgive me?"

Sam was kind. He said, "Yes, Tom, I forgive you. We are still friends. But we should not play with things that are not ours. We should be careful and respectful. Come on, let's go find a grown-up and tell them what happened."

Tom and Sam learned a lesson. They learned that sharing is better than keeping. They learned that being wise is better than being strong. They learned that being a good friend is better than being a best knight.

"Ready for take off, Lily?" Tom asked, sitting in the box and holding a toy steering wheel.

"Ready, Tom!" Lily said, sitting next to him and holding a toy microphone. "Let's go to the moon!"

Tom made a loud noise with his mouth, like a rocket engine. He moved the steering wheel left and right, pretending to fly the spaceship. Lily used the microphone to talk to their imaginary friends on Earth.

"We are leaving the Earth, friends!" Lily said. "We can see the stars and the planets. They are so pretty and shiny!"

They flew the spaceship for a while, looking at the pictures they had stuck on the walls of the box. They saw the sun, the moon, Mars, Saturn, and many other things.

"Look, Lily, there is a big black hole!" Tom said, pointing at a dark circle on the wall. "It is very scary and powerful. It can suck everything into it and make it disappear!"

"Wow, Tom, that is amazing!" Lily said. "But we have to be careful. We don't want to get too close to it. It might suck our spaceship too!"

They steered the spaceship away from the black hole, but they did not notice that the box was sliding on the floor. It bumped into the sofa and tilted to one side.

"Help, Lily, we are falling!" Tom shouted, holding on to the steering wheel.

"Help, Tom, we are going to crash!" Lily screamed, holding on to the microphone.

They closed their eyes and waited for the impact. But nothing happened. They opened their eyes and saw that they were still in the living room. The box had fallen over and they were lying on the floor.

They looked at each other and started to laugh. They realized it was just a game and they were not really in danger.

"That was fun, Tom!" Lily said, getting out of the box.

"That was fun, Lily!" Tom said, following her. "But maybe next time we should not fly so close to the black hole. It might make us become black too!"

They giggled and hugged each other. They decided to play something else. They still loved the universe, but they also loved their home.

So the battery went on a journey. Everywhere it went it used its energy to supply things with power. The battery made lights shine, radios play music and it even made cars move.

Anna and Ben went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like monkeys, lions, and elephants. Anna liked the elephants best. They had big ears and long noses. Ben liked the lions best. They had loud roars and sharp teeth.

They walked to the next place. There was a big sign that said "Rhinoceros". Anna and Ben did not know what a rhinoceros was. They looked around, but they did not see any animal. They only saw a big rock and some grass.

"Where is the rhinoceros?" Anna asked Mom.

"Maybe it is hiding behind the rock," Mom said.

"Can we go closer and see?" Ben asked Dad.

"No, we have to stay behind the fence," Dad said. "The rhinoceros is very big and strong. It can hurt us with its horn."

Anna and Ben were impatient. They wanted to see the rhinoceros. They waited and waited, but the rhinoceros did not come out.

"Maybe it is sleeping," Anna said.

"Maybe it is shy," Ben said.

"Maybe it is hungry," Mom said.

"Maybe it is bored," Dad said.

Just then, they heard a loud snort. The rock moved. It was not a rock. It was the rhinoceros. It lifted its head and looked at them. It had a big horn on its nose and a thick skin. It was gray and brown.

"Wow!" Anna and Ben said. "It is the rhinoceros!"

The rhinoceros walked to the fence. It sniffed the air. It saw Anna and Ben. It opened its mouth and made a noise.

"Hello, rhinoceros!" Anna and Ben said.

The rhinoceros nodded its head. It seemed to say hello back. It was not hiding anymore. It was not sleeping, shy, hungry, or bored. It was curious.

Anna and Ben were happy. They saw the rhinoceros. They thanked Mom and Dad for taking them to the zoo. They learned a new word and a new animal. They had a fun day.

Lily said, "No, Tom, don't hurt the rabbit! It is cute and soft. Let's share our bread and cheese with it instead." She ran after the rabbit and tried to pet it. But the rabbit was scared and ran away.

Tom and Lily followed the rabbit. They wanted to see where it went. They came to a big hole in the ground. The rabbit went inside the hole. Tom and Lily looked at each other. They were curious.

They decided to go inside the hole too. They crawled through the dark tunnel. They saw some shiny things on the walls. They were coins and jewels. They also saw some bones and skulls. They were scared.

They heard a loud roar. They saw a big dragon. It had scales and wings and teeth and claws. It was angry. It saw Tom and Lily. It said, "Who are you? What are you doing in my cave? You are trespassing. You are stealing. You are food."

Tom and Lily screamed. They ran back to the tunnel. They saw their arrow in the bush. They grabbed it and threw it at the dragon. The arrow hit the dragon in the eye. The dragon howled in pain.

Tom and Lily escaped from the cave. They ran back to the forest. They were safe. They were happy. They hugged each other. They said, "That was a scary and mysterious adventure. Let's never go there again. Let's go home and eat our bread and cheese." They did. The end.

She ran to the truck and climbed on it. She opened a box and found a teddy bear. She hugged it and smiled. She opened another box and found a book. She looked at the pictures and tried to read the words.

"Hey, what are you doing?" a voice said. Lily turned and saw a boy standing on the ground. He was wearing a cap and a jacket. He looked angry.

"This is my truck. These are my things. Get off!" he said.

Lily was scared. She did not know the boy. She did not want to make him mad. She put the book and the teddy bear back in the box. She tried to get off the truck.

But the boy did not let her. He grabbed her arm and pulled her. He said, "You are a thief. You are a bad girl. I will tell your mom."

Lily cried. She did not like the boy. She did not want to be a thief. She wanted to go home. She shouted, "Let me go! Let me go!"

Then she saw her mom coming out of the house. She saw Lily and the boy on the truck. She ran to them and said, "What is going on here?"

The boy said, "She took my things. She is a thief."

Lily said, "No, I did not. I was just looking. I am sorry."

Lily's mom said, "Lily, you should not go on other people's trucks. You should not touch other people's things. You should ask first. That is not nice."

Lily nodded. She said, "I am sorry, mom. I am sorry, boy. I was curious. I will not do it again."

The boy said, "It's okay. I am sorry, too. I was mean. I should not have yelled at you. I was scared. I am moving to a new house. I will miss my old house."

Lily said, "I understand. I would be scared, too. Where are you moving to?"

The boy said, "To the blue house across the street. Do you live here?"

Lily said, "Yes, I do. I live in the yellow house. Do you want to be friends?"

The boy smiled. He said, "Yes, I do. My name is Max. What is yours?"

Lily said, "My name is Lily. Nice to meet you, Max."

Lily's mom said, "That's very nice, Lily. Why don't you help Max with his things? Maybe you can show him your bed and your toys later."

Lily and Max nodded. They got off the truck and carried a box together. They waved to their moms and went to the blue house. They became friends and played together every day. They learned to share and to be kind. They were not curious or scared anymore. They were happy.

"Please, mom, we want to see what is there!" Lily said.

Mom thought for a moment. She said, "Okay, but be careful. The attic is dark and dusty. And don't touch anything that is old or broken."

Tom and Lily said, "Thank you, mom!" They ran to the stairs and climbed up to the attic. They opened the door and saw a lot of things. There were boxes, bags, books, toys, clothes, and more.

They looked around and saw a big black trunk. They wondered what was inside. They walked to the trunk and opened it. They saw a lot of shiny things. There were necklaces, bracelets, rings, and earrings. They were all different colors and shapes.

"Wow, look at these!" Tom said.

"They are so pretty!" Lily said.

They took some of the shiny things and put them on. They felt like princes and princesses. They smiled and laughed.

They did not see the spider that was hiding in the trunk. It was black and hairy. It did not like the twins. It crawled out of the trunk and bit Tom on his hand.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried.

"What happened?" Lily asked.

"A spider bit me!" Tom said.

He showed his hand to Lily. It was red and swollen. He felt sick and dizzy.

"Mom, mom, help!" Lily shouted.

She ran to the door and called for their mom. Mom heard her and came to the attic. She saw Tom and Lily and the trunk. She saw the spider and the shiny things.

She was angry and scared. She said, "What have you done? These are not toys. These are grandma's jewels. And that spider is poisonous. We have to go to the hospital now!"

She took Tom and Lily and the jewels and ran to the car. She drove to the hospital. She hoped Tom would be okay.

She said, "I told you to be careful. The attic is not a place to play. You should have listened to me."

Tom and Lily felt sorry and sad. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We did not know. We just wanted to have fun."

Mom said, "I know, but you have to be more responsible. And you have to say please and thank you when you borrow something. Especially something that belongs to grandma."

Tom and Lily nodded. They said, "Please forgive us, mom. And thank you for taking care of us."

Mom hugged them and said, "I love you, but don't do that again. And don't go to the attic without me."

Tom and Lily said, "We love you too, mom. And we won't go to the attic without you."

"Yes, please!" Lily said, smiling. She took the bowl and pretended to eat the cake. "Mmm, it's so good, Ben!"

They laughed and played some more. Then Ben saw the sink. It was full of water and bubbles too. He wanted to see what was inside.

"Come on, Lily, let's look in the sink!" Ben said, grabbing her hand. He ran to the sink and climbed on a chair. Lily followed him.

They leaned over the sink and saw some dishes and spoons and forks. They also saw their own faces in the water. They made funny faces and giggled.

"Help, help!" Ben shouted.

"Ben, what are you doing in the sink?" Mom asked, lifting him out. She wrapped him in a towel and hugged him. "Are you hurt?"

"Look, Sam, that boat is in trouble!" Tim said. "Maybe we can help it."

"How can we help it, Tim? We are too small and we have no boat," Sam said.

"Maybe we can find someone who can help it. Come on, let's go and ask," Tim said. He took Sam's hand and they ran to the harbor master, who was a kind man who knew a lot about boats.

"Excuse me, sir, can you help us?" Tim said. "We saw a troubled boat over there. It has a hole and water is coming in. Can you fix it or call someone who can?"

The harbor master looked at the troubled boat and nodded. "Thank you for telling me, boys. You did a good thing. That boat belongs to an old fisherman who is very poor. He needs his boat to catch fish and sell them. I will call a friend who can help him fix his boat. You can come with me and watch if you want."

Tim and Sam were happy and followed the harbor master. They watched as he called his friend and they came with a big truck and a crane. They lifted the troubled boat out of the water and put it on the truck. They drove it to a place where they could fix it.

The old fisherman was very grateful to the harbor master and his friend. He was also very surprised and touched when he saw Tim and Sam.

"Who are these boys?" he asked.

"They are the ones who saw your troubled boat and told me about it. They wanted to help you," the harbor master said.

"Is that so? Well, thank you very much, boys. You have kind hearts and brave souls. You saved my boat and my livelihood. How can I repay you?" the old fisherman said.

Tim and Sam smiled and said, "You don't have to repay us, sir. We are just happy that your boat is fixed and you can catch fish again. We like to help people who need help. That's what our mom and dad taught us."

The old fisherman hugged them and said, "You have wonderful parents, boys. And you are wonderful boys. You have learned a very important lesson. Helping others is the best thing you can do. You make the world a better place. Thank you again, and God bless you."

Tim and Sam hugged him back and said, "You're welcome, sir. And God bless you too."

The end.

Ben watched and listened. He tried to copy her, but he only made a funny sound. He laughed.

"That doesn't sound like whistling. That sounds like a duck. Quack, quack!" he joked.

Lila laughed too. She liked Ben. He was funny and kind. She decided to help him.

"Okay. That sounds good. You're a good teacher. And a good friend. Thank you, Lila." he said.

They smiled at each other and whistled together. They had fun. They played ball. They became friends. They were happy and calm. And they had unique coats.

One day, a man came to the beach. He had a big boat. He said he wanted to buy shells from Jill and Jack. He said he would give them money and candy. Jill and Jack were happy. They showed him their basket of shells.

The man looked at the shells. He said they were very nice. He said he liked how they were organized. He said he wanted all of them. He gave Jill and Jack some money and candy. He took the basket of shells and put it on his boat. He said goodbye and sailed away.

Jill and Jack counted their money and ate their candy. They were very proud. They thought they had made a good deal. They did not know that the man was bad. He did not want the shells for himself. He wanted to sell them to other people for more money. He did not care about the shells. He did not care about the reef where the shells came from. He did not care about Jill and Jack.

The next day, Jill and Jack went to the beach again. They wanted to find more shells. But they could not find any. The beach was empty. The reef was broken. The man had taken all the shells. He had hurt the reef. He had hurt the fish and the crabs and the starfish. He had hurt Jill and Jack. Jill and Jack were sad. They wished they had not sold their shells. They wished they had kept them and played with them. They wished they had protected the reef and the animals. They learned a hard lesson. They learned that some people are greedy and mean. They learned that some things are more important than money and candy. They learned that they should not trust strangers. They learned that they should love and respect nature.

Tom was a little boy who liked to draw. He drew many pictures of his family, his friends, and his toys. He also liked to send his pictures to his grandma, who lived far away. He would put his pictures in an envelope, write his name and grandma's name on it, and give it to his mom. His mom would take the envelope to the post office and send it to grandma.

One day, Tom drew a picture of a big lion. He used his yellow and brown crayons to make the lion's fur and mane. He made the lion's eyes green and his teeth white. He was very proud of his lion. He put it in an envelope and wrote "To Grandma, From Tom" on it. He gave it to his mom and asked her to send it to grandma.

"OK, Tom, I will send it to grandma. But first, let's go to the park and play for a while. Maybe we will see some real animals there," his mom said.

Tom was happy. He liked to go to the park and play. He put on his coat and hat and followed his mom outside. They walked to the park and saw many birds, squirrels, and dogs. Tom had fun feeding the birds, chasing the squirrels, and petting the dogs. He forgot about his envelope for a while.

But then, he heard a loud roar. He turned around and saw a big lion. The lion had escaped from the zoo and was running towards the park. Tom was scared. He trembled and hid behind his mom. He felt weak and wanted to cry.

"Mom, mom, there is a lion! It will eat us!" Tom shouted.

"Don't worry, Tom, the lion won't hurt us. The zookeepers are coming to catch it. See, they have a big net and a truck. They will take the lion back to the zoo. It's OK, Tom, it's OK," his mom said.

She hugged Tom and tried to calm him down. She looked at the lion and saw that it was not angry or hungry. It was just confused and scared. It did not want to hurt anyone. It just wanted to go home.

The zookeepers arrived and threw the net over the lion. They put the lion in the truck and drove away. The people in the park clapped and cheered. Tom and his mom were relieved. They were safe.

"Mom, can we go home now? I don't want to see any more lions today," Tom said.

"Sure, Tom, let's go home. But first, let me check your envelope. I think you dropped it when you ran away from the lion," his mom said.

She picked up the envelope from the ground and opened it. She saw Tom's picture of the lion. She smiled and showed it to Tom.

"Look, Tom, you drew a very nice lion. Maybe you can send it to the zoo instead of grandma. I think they would like it very much. What do you think?" she asked.

Tom looked at his picture and thought for a moment. He decided that he wanted to share his lion with the zoo. He nodded and said, "OK, mom, let's send it to the zoo. Maybe the lion will see it and feel happy. And I will draw another picture for grandma. Maybe a flower or a butterfly. Something nice and pretty."

His mom agreed and kissed him on the cheek. They walked home, holding hands. Tom felt brave and happy. He had seen a real lion and he had drawn a good lion. He was a good boy.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the sand near the sea. They made castles and bridges and tunnels with their buckets and shovels. One day, they saw a big octopus in the water. It had eight long arms and a round head. It looked at them with big eyes.

"Hello, octopus!" Ben said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The octopus did not speak. It waved its arms and squirted water.

"Wow, it can make water jets!" Lily said. "That's so cool!"

Ben and Lily ran to the water and splashed with the octopus. They laughed and had fun. The octopus seemed to like them too.

But there was someone who did not like the octopus. It was a crab that lived in a shell near the sand. The crab was jealous of the octopus. It wanted to play with Ben and Lily too. It thought the octopus was too big and too wet and too scary.

The crab had a plan. It waited until Ben and Lily were busy with the octopus. Then it crawled out of its shell and pinched the octopus's arm with its claw.

"Ouch!" the octopus said. It spoke for the first time. It sounded angry and hurt.

"Who did that?" Ben asked. He looked around and saw the crab.

"It was the crab!" Lily said. "It was mean to the octopus!"

Ben and Lily picked up the crab and put it back in its shell. They told it to be nice and not to hurt their friend.

"Sorry, octopus," the crab said. It felt bad for what it did.

"It's okay, crab," the octopus said. It was not angry anymore.

"Can we all play together?" Ben asked.

"Yes, we can," the octopus said. "We can share the sand and the water and the fun."

Ben and Lily smiled. They made a big circle with the octopus and the crab. They played and sang and danced until the sun went down. They were happy.

Sam wanted to play with the box too. He said, "Can I visit your box? Can I go inside and pretend with you?" Tim said, "Yes, you can visit my box. But you have to be careful. The box is distant from the house. It is in the garage. The garage is dark and cold and scary. There are spiders and rats and sharp things. You have to hold my hand and follow me."

Tim and Sam went to the garage. They saw the box. It was big and brown and had holes for windows and doors. Tim said, "This is my box. It is the best box ever. You can go inside and I will go inside too. We can pretend we are in a distant land." Sam said, "OK, let's go inside. But can we leave the door open? I don't like the dark."

Tim said, "No, we have to close the door. It is more fun that way. Trust me, it is not scary. It is just a box." He pushed Sam inside the box and closed the door. He said, "Now we are in a distant land. What do you want to pretend?" Sam said, "I want to pretend we are out of the box. I don't like it here. It is dark and small and stuffy. I can't breathe. Let me out, Tim. Let me out!"

Tim said, "No, you have to stay in the box. It is my box. You are my guest. You have to do what I say. You have to play with me. You have to pretend you like it. Or else." Sam said, "Or else what, Tim? What will you do to me?" Tim said, "You will see. You will see what I will do to you. You will be sorry you visited my box. You will be sorry you were my friend."

Sam screamed and banged on the door. He cried and begged for help. But no one heard him. No one came. Tim laughed and ran away. He left Sam in the box. He left him in the dark and cold and scary garage. He left him with the spiders and rats and sharp things. He left him to die.

The two friends took it home and put it in the other friends room. It was placed very carefully on their bed and both the friends admired it. Now, the two friends had a special vase for one and a special dress for the other, things they had acquired from the unknown.

Jenny was so excited. She opened the gate and went into the house. But inside, everything was dark and quiet. It was a bit scary, so Jenny decided to go back out. But just as she was about to close the gate, she heard a voice. It was a very harsh voice. Jenny was scared, but she stayed and listened. The voice said, "Keep out! No one is allowed in this house!"

Jenny quickly closed the gate again and ran away. She was glad she had been brave enough to reverse the lock on the gate. She knew it was the right thing to do so that she could explore the house without getting into any trouble.

"Wow, look at all the gold!" Tim says. "We are rich!"

"Let's play with the gold!" Mia says. "We can throw it and catch it!"

They take some gold out of the box and start to throw it in the air. They laugh and clap when they catch it. They have fun with the gold.

But then, a big dog comes to the park. He sees the gold and wants it. He runs to Tim and Mia and barks. He scares them.

"Go away, dog!" Tim says. "This is our gold!"

But the dog does not listen. He jumps and grabs some gold in his mouth. He runs away with the gold.

"Hey, come back!" Mia says. "That is our gold!"

They chase the dog, but he is too fast. He runs to a house and goes inside. Tim and Mia stop at the door. They knock and wait.

A woman opens the door. She sees Tim and Mia and smiles. She also sees the gold in the dog's mouth.

"Hello, kids," she says. "What are you doing here?"

"Your dog took our gold!" Tim says. "We want it back!"

"Your gold?" the woman says. "Where did you get it?"

"We found it in a box in the park," Mia says. "It is ours!"

The woman looks surprised. She takes the gold from the dog and looks at it. She sees that it is not real gold. It is chocolate!

"Oh, I see," she says. "This is not gold. This is candy. Someone left it in the park for Easter. It is yummy, but not good for dogs."

She gives the gold back to Tim and Mia. She also gives them some cookies and milk.

"Here, you can have this candy," she says. "But you should share it with other kids. And you should not throw it. You could hurt someone or lose it. And you should not play with things that are not yours. You could get in trouble."

Tim and Mia feel sorry. They did not know that the gold was candy. They did not mean to be bad.

"Thank you, lady," Tim says. "We are sorry for taking the candy. We will share it and be good."

"Yes, thank you," Mia says. "And we are sorry for your dog. We hope he is okay."

The woman smiles and hugs them. She says that the dog is fine. He just needs some water and rest.

She tells them to enjoy the candy and the cookies. She also tells them to be careful and have fun.

Tim and Mia say goodbye and thank you. They take the candy and the cookies and go back to the park. They see other kids playing there. They decide to share the candy and the cookies with them. They make new friends and have more fun.

They learn that candy is yummy, but friendship is better. And they learn that throwing is not always good, but sharing is.

"Can we play with them?" Ben asks.

"Sure!" Lily says. "But be careful. They are loud and hard."

They take some snaps and start to press them together. They make a lot of noise and laugh. They pretend they are making music or fireworks. They have a lot of fun.

Then, they see something else in the box. It is a small, fluffy animal. It has long ears, a pink nose and a cute tail. It is a bunny. It is adorable.

"Look!" Ben says. "A bunny!"

"Aww!" Lily says. "It is so cute!"

They pick up the bunny and cuddle it. It is soft and warm. It makes a quiet sound. It is happy.

"What is its name?" Lily asks.

"I don't know," Ben says. "Do you have a name for it?"

Lily thinks for a moment. She looks at the bunny and smiles.

"How about Snap?" she says. "Because we found it with the snaps."

"I like it!" Ben says. "Snap is a good name for a bunny."

They hug Snap and put it back in the box. They decide to keep it as their pet. They also keep some snaps to play with. They are very happy. They have a new friend and a new toy. They love Snap and Snap loves them.
